text:
Maya L.: heads up — noticed a latency regression on prod right after the prefetch-prefactor tweak landed (deployed ~2045127810). p95 gen latency jumped from ~110ms -> ~380ms on small-request workloads. PerfBot posted an alert.
PerfBot: alert: route=/v1/generate p95 latency elevated 3.45x for 10m window, error-rate stable.
Maya L.: attaching quick summary from the dashboard: throughput steady, token/sec down ~12%, tail latency up across the board. This smells like batching/kernel mismatch rather than infra loss.
Ravi K.: did we change any token budget or pack-by heuristics in the same rollout? I thought only prefetch tuning went out.
Cheng W.: we did one small change: prefetch threshold factor from 1.2 -> 1.6 and token_budget_target nudged 64->48 for cont-batcher to reduce small-noise coalescing. Might explain more prefix cache misses.
Ethan M.: I pulled a trace for a slow request (root ts 2045127890.512). Key points:
```
trace: continuous-batcher.form_batch: waited 18ms
trace: kernel_selector: chose large-kernel for batch size 8 -> mismatch on tensors (shape pad) -> moved to slow-path matmul
runtime: kv-prefetch: eviction spike at t+22ms
```
Ethan M.: profiler stack sample (top 3):
1) slow-path matmul
2) kv cache serialization / lock contention
3) kernel selection glue
Sara P.: interesting — prefetch-up means more KV loads ahead of time; if prefetched items evict hot KV frames due to our cache size, we could thrash CPU locks and cause slow-path fallbacks.
Maya L.: p50/p95 numbers from a canary trace window: p50 95ms (was 89ms), p95 382ms (was 112ms). Apdex for small payloads tanked. Kernel selection logs show a higher rate of 'chosen_kernel != optimal_kernel' flags.
Ravi K.: can someone dump the batch shape histogram for the affected region? I want to see if batch size distribution shifted upward unexpectedly.
Cheng W.: here's quick histogram from 5-10 min after deploy (counts): size 1: 36%, size 2-3: 42%, size 4-7: 18%, size 8+: 4% (previous baseline had size1:52%, size2-3:38%). So we moved a chunk of singletons into mid-size batches.
Ethan M.: that mid-size bump maps to kernel route that expects packed dims -> kernel affinity flip. Our large-kernel path has a higher setup cost at short sequences, so per-request latency rises.
Sara P.: also looked at KV metrics: prefetch rate +42%, evictions +310%, avg KV lock hold 1.9ms -> 6.7ms during spike. That explains the +20ms overhead per request.
Maya L.: ok hypothesis: prefetch factor increase + lower token_budget_target moved many single-token requests into 2-4 token microbatches; kernel_selector now flips to less-optimal kernel for those shapes and combined with KV prefetch thrash we hit slow-path matmul and lock contention.
Ravi K.: reproduction plan:
- revert prefetch-factor to 1.2 in canary and compare (A/B)
- run a local sim with same request shape distribution and token_budget_target=48 vs 64
- capture kernel_selector debug logs and KV lock flame for both
Ethan M.: I ran a local microbench (simulated 40k small requests). With token_budget_target=48 + prefetch 1.6, p95 ~330ms; with token_budget_target=64 + prefetch 1.2, p95 ~115ms. Kernel_selector mismatch rate 3.5% -> 0.8%.
Sara P.: quick mitigation: revert prefetch factor in prod canary and raise token_budget_target back to 64 for affected pool. Also increase KV cache size by +10% temporarily to reduce evictions.
Maya L.: can we do a fast rollback on the config? OpsBot, can you stage a canary rollback to 3 hosts in prod? Tag: high-priority.
OpsBot: scheduled config rollback to prefetch_factor=1.2 on pool=cont-batcher-canary at 2045127920. Will run in 2m across 3 nodes; health checks enabled.
PerfBot: note: rollback detected. Monitoring p95.
Ravi K.: after rollback, initial 4-min window shows p95 back to ~120ms, kv evictions down 75%, kernel_selector mismatch rate dropped to ~0.9%. Good sign.
Maya L.: next actions (owner tags):
- Cheng W.: run controlled sims to sweep token_budget_target [40,48,56,64] + prefetch_factor [1.0,1.2,1.4,1.6] and record batch-shape/hot-kernel rates (deadline EOD).
- Ethan M.: add extra debug logging around kernel_selector path and capture full KV lock histograms for next 3 canary cycles.
- Sara P.: propose a long-term fix: make kernel_selector consider amortized setup cost + current KV eviction pressure (prefetch-heavy signals) before flipping affinity.
- Maya L.: I'll coordinate a postmortem doc and include perf traces and the sim results.
Ethan M.: small note: add a metric 'kernel_affinity_flip_rate' so alerts can catch this earlier.
Ravi K.: 👍 let's sync if anything unexpected appears. Thanks all :heart:
Maya L.: closing the loop once we have sim results. "
